\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Absolute-value invariance of the uniform norm]
\lean{FABL.uniformLpNorm_abs}
\label{FABL.uniformLpNorm_abs}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformLpNorm}
\difficulty{3}
For a finite nonempty set $\Omega$, a real number $p$, and a function
$f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$, the uniform $L^p$ quantity of the function $x\mapsto |f(x)|$
equals that of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reduction to nonnegative functions]
\lean{FABL.exercise9_7_nonnegative_reduction}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p271-b006}
\label{FABL.exercise9_7_nonnegative_reduction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.abs_noiseOperator_le_noiseOperator_abs, FABL.noiseOperator, FABL.noiseOperator_nonneg, FABL.uniformLpNorm, FABL.uniformLpNorm_abs, FABL.uniformLpNorm_le_of_abs_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p,q,\rho$ be real numbers with $p>0$, $q>0$, and
$-1\leq\rho\leq1$, and suppose that for every pointwise nonnegative function
$g:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, the noise operator with parameter $\rho$ satisfies $\|T_\rho
g\|_q\leq\|g\|_p$. Then the same inequality holds for every real-valued function $f$ on
$\{\pm1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}
